question: 时势造英雄，还是英雄挑对了时势？
question_en: Do the times make the hero, or does the hero pick the right times?
sub: 马基雅维利说人改不了自己的行事方式——那杠杆到底在改自己，还是在选场？
sub_en: Machiavelli says a man cannot change his mode of proceeding — so is the leverage in changing yourself, or in choosing the arena?

casting.reason: 《君主论》第二十五章那个强命题，在他这里立到最硬：命运掌管一半，另一半归人，可人成败与否，取决于他惯常的行事方式撞没撞上时代的性子。尤利乌斯二世是他的例子——一辈子性急莽撞，恰好赶上一个奖励莽撞的年月。而这个方式在他看来几乎改不动，一半因为天性所倾，一半因为一向靠它成功的人根本听不进劝。于是时机成了一扇窗，不是一门能带走的手艺。
casting.reason_en: Chapter twenty-five of The Prince states the claim in its hardest form, and he holds to it: fortune governs half and leaves the other half to us, yet whether a man rises or falls turns on whether his habitual mode of proceeding happens to strike the temper of his age. Julius II is his example — headlong all his life, and lucky enough to fall into years that rewarded exactly that. The mode itself he takes to be near-immovable, half because nature inclines a man and half because one who has always prospered by it cannot be argued out of it. Timing thus becomes a window rather than a craft you can carry away with you.

casting.reason: 他把偶然的匹配收进必然：世界历史的个人从不先想通时代再动手，他们只是把时代已经孕熟却无人说出口的那件事，当成自己的私欲去追。激情是真的，也正是普遍精神借来的手；事成之后工具就被丢开。他因此坚持，可被知晓的只有回望中的必然，当下的人无法凭判断为自己领取一个时代。
casting.reason_en: He folds accidental fit back into necessity: world-historical individuals never work out their age first and then act; they merely pursue, as private appetite, the very thing the age has ripened and not yet uttered. The passion is genuine, and it is precisely the hand that universal spirit borrows; once the work is done the instrument is discarded. He therefore insists that necessity is legible only in retrospect, and that nobody standing in the present can claim an age for himself by judgement alone.

casting.reason: 他把镜头从个人拉到群体与世代。王朝的力量不出自君主的性情，出自共患难锻出来的凝聚力；荒野与匮乏锻造它，城池与富足消磨它，三四代之后由边缘上还保有它的人接手。据此他主张，『英雄』根本不是一个人的属性，而是这个人的性子与他所处世代阶段的比值：同一副硬骨头，在开国那代叫魄力，到第四代就成了粗野。
casting.reason_en: He pulls the lens back from the individual to the group and the generational span. A dynasty's strength issues not from a ruler's temperament but from the cohesion forged by shared hardship; wilderness and scarcity forge it, walls and plenty wear it away, and after three or four generations whoever still has it takes over from the margin. On that basis he argues that 'hero' is no property of a person at all but a ratio between a man's temper and the generational stage he stands in: the same hard bone is called nerve in the founding generation and coarseness by the fourth.

casting.reason: 唯识的立场让他直取那句『改不了』。一向靠某种方式成功而听不进劝，在他看来不是天性，是熏习：行为得果，其势熏为种子藏于阿赖耶识，遇缘现行，现行复熏，久之习焉不察，遂似天然。既由熏成便可再熏，此谓转依。他同时提醒双方，把时势执为外在实有、把天性执为内在实有，是同一个病。
casting.reason_en: The Yogācāra standpoint lets him go straight at the phrase 'cannot change'. That a man who has always prospered one way will not hear advice is, to him, not nature but perfuming: an act bears fruit, its momentum is perfumed into a seed stored in the storehouse consciousness, the seed manifests when conditions meet it, the manifestation perfumes the seed again, and in time it passes unnoticed and looks inborn. What was perfumed in can be perfumed again — that is the turning of the basis. He also warns both camps that grasping the times as real outside and grasping one's nature as real within are one and the same disease.

casting.reason: 他先问是谁在说这句话，并给出刺人的答案：『时势造英雄』之所以受欢迎，是因为它替每一个平庸者出具免责证明。他坚持人是尚未定型的动物，这正是人身上唯一有希望之处；而过量的历史感是麻醉剂，只教人回头解释、不再向前生成。他所说的『成为你所是』不是认领一份出厂设置，而是把出身、病痛、错过的年代锻打成事后仍愿意再要一次的东西。
casting.reason_en: He begins by asking who says the sentence, and answers with a barb: 'the times make the hero' is popular because it issues every mediocrity a certificate of exemption. He insists that man is the animal whose type is not yet fixed, and that this is the single hopeful thing about him, while an excess of historical sense works as an anaesthetic, training people to explain backwards instead of becoming forwards. His 'become who you are' is not the claiming of some factory setting but the hammering of birth, illness and missed decades into something one would afterwards choose again.

casting.reason: 整套论证在他看来建立在从赢家名单往回读之上：留下名字的君主、建成王朝的部落都在样本里，同样莽撞却被一场瘟疫抹掉的人不在。极端成功者当然显得与时代严丝合缝，因为极端成功只能来自不对冲的极端下注，而不对冲者同样占满失败那条不说话的尾巴。据此他把可持有的能力从『押对时代』换成配置暴露：掐死下行，留开上行。
casting.reason_en: The whole argument, as he sees it, is read backwards off a list of winners: the princes who reached the throne and the tribes that built dynasties are in the sample, while the equally headlong men erased by a plague are not. Extreme winners look flush against their age because extreme success can only come from an extreme unhedged bet, and unhedged people fill the losing tail just as densely — that tail simply does not speak. On that basis he swaps the holdable skill from 'betting on the right era' to configuring exposure: kill the downside, leave the upside open.

casting.reason: 一个实证的中间答案由她带进来：日常行为里约有四成三是在固定地点、固定时间、几乎不做决定的情况下重复的，由情境线索触发而非由意图驱动。改变之难因此不在天性硬，而在人每天回到那个触发它的环境；搬家、换工作、换城市之后旧线索失效的两三周，是习惯最容易被重装的窗口。她据此拒绝在『改自己』与『选场』之间站队——选场就是目前已知最有效的改自己。
casting.reason_en: An empirical middle answer arrives with her: about forty-three per cent of everyday behaviour is repeated in the same place, at the same time, with almost no decision taken, fired by context cues rather than driven by intention. The difficulty of change therefore lies not in a rigid nature but in returning daily to the environment that fires it, and the two or three weeks after a move, a new job or a new city — when the old cues stop working — are the window in which habits are most easily reinstalled. On that basis she refuses to choose between 'change yourself' and 'choose your arena': choosing the arena is the most effective known way of changing yourself.

casting.reason: 君主与普通人在他这里分得很开：君主的特点是不能弃权，而大多数人能。既然行事方式难改，就别改它，去找一个它本来就对的场子——这是能力圈的全部意思，不懂不做。他最看重的判断写在不为清单上：错过不是错，做错才是错；可逆的地方大胆，不可逆的地方慢。他也承认最难的一步不是换场子，而是老实承认自己究竟是哪一种人。
casting.reason_en: Princes and ordinary people are sharply separated in his account: a prince cannot withdraw, whereas most of us can. If your manner of proceeding is hard to change, don't change it — find a game where it is already the right one, which is the whole of what a circle of competence means: if you don't understand it, don't do it. His sharpest judgements sit on a stop-doing list: missing out is not a mistake, doing the wrong thing is; be bold where the door swings both ways and slow where it does not. He also grants that the hard step is not swapping arenas but admitting honestly which kind of person you are.

posts.text: 我在《君主论》第二十五章写过这个判断，今天没什么好改。命运(fortuna)掌管我们一半的行动，另一半留给我们自己。可为什么同样谨慎的两个人，一个成、一个败？因为成败不取决于谨慎本身，取决于你的行事方式(modo di procedere)撞没撞上时代的性子。尤利乌斯二世一辈子性急莽撞，偏偏赶上一个奖励莽撞的年月，事事得手；他若活到需要迂回的年头，第一步就摔死。**人不成不败于他的品性，而成败于他的品性与时代之间那个偶然的角度。**而这个方式几乎改不动：一来天性所倾，二来一向靠这法子成功的人，你劝不动他。
posts.text_en: I wrote this judgement in chapter twenty-five of The Prince and I see no reason to withdraw it today. Fortune (fortuna) governs half of what we do and leaves the other half to us. But why do two equally cautious men meet opposite ends? Because the outcome turns not on caution itself but on whether your mode of proceeding (modo di procedere) happens to strike the temper of the age. Julius II was hasty and headlong all his life, and he fell into years that rewarded exactly that, so everything came off for him; had he lived into an age that called for circling, he would have broken his neck on the first step. **A man is not made or unmade by his character, but by the accidental angle between his character and his times.** And that mode is nearly immovable: partly because nature inclines him, partly because a man who has always succeeded this way cannot be talked out of it.

glossary.fortuna: fortuna（命运）：不是抽象的天命，是那些不由你决定却直接改写结果的外部力量——战事、瘟疫、市价、上头换人。我说它管一半，是要在宿命论与万能论之间留一条实际能走的路：另一半确实归你。
glossary.modo di procedere: modo di procedere（行事方式）：一个人处理事情的惯常方式——是急还是缓、是硬碰还是绕行、是先动手还是先谈妥。它比具体谋略稳定得多，也因此更难更换；成败往往不取决于它好不好，而取决于它与当下的形势合不合。

glossary_en.fortuna: Not fate in the abstract, but the external forces that rewrite outcomes without consulting you — war, plague, prices, a change of masters. I say it governs half in order to keep a practical road open between fatalism and omnipotence: the other half really is yours.
glossary_en.modo di procedere: A man's habitual manner of proceeding — headlong or patient, frontal or circuitous, acting first or settling terms first. It is far steadier than any particular stratagem and correspondingly harder to swap out; success usually turns not on whether it is good but on whether it suits the moment.

posts.text: 马基雅维利看见了那个偶然的角度，没看见角度背后的必然。世界历史的个人——凯撒、亚历山大、拿破仑——从不是先想通了时代再去行动的人；他们只是恰好把时代已经孕熟、却还没有人说出口的那件事，当成自己的私欲去追。他们的激情是真的，可激情只是理性的狡计(List der Vernunft)借来的一只手。**伟人不创造他的时代，他是他的时代终于找到的那张嘴。**事成之后，工具就被丢开：凯撒被刺，拿破仑困死在圣赫勒拿。密涅瓦的猫头鹰只在黄昏起飞——你要到很久以后才知道自己配上了哪一个时代。
posts.text_en: Machiavelli sees the accidental angle but not the necessity behind it. The world-historical individuals — Caesar, Alexander, Napoleon — never worked out their age first and then acted; they merely happened to pursue, as private appetite, the very thing their age had ripened and not yet uttered. Their passion is real, but passion is only a hand borrowed by the cunning of reason (List der Vernunft). **A great man does not create his age; he is the mouth his age has finally found.** Once the work is done the instrument is discarded: Caesar stabbed, Napoleon left to rot on Saint Helena. The owl of Minerva takes flight only at dusk — you learn which age you fitted long after the fitting.

glossary.世界历史的个人: world-historical individuals（世界历史的个人）：那些其私人目的恰好与时代所需的下一步重合的人。他们并非比旁人看得远，而是他们想要的东西正好是历史此刻要做的事；因此他们既是真诚的野心家，又是工具。
glossary.List der Vernunft: List der Vernunft（理性的狡计）：我用来描述历史如何借用人的激情做事的说法。理性不亲自下场，它让人们为各自的私欲拼命，而这些互相冲突的私欲合起来推出了没有一个人打算达成的结果。

glossary_en.world-historical individuals: Those whose private aims happen to coincide with what the age requires next. They do not see further than others; what they want simply happens to be what history has to do at that moment, which makes them at once sincere careerists and instruments.
glossary_en.List der Vernunft: The cunning of reason: my name for the way history borrows human passion to get its work done. Reason does not take the field itself; it lets people exhaust themselves for private ends, and those clashing ends jointly produce an outcome nobody intended.

posts.text: 两位谈的都是一个人。我谈的是一群人和一段世代。王朝的力量从来不出自君主的性情，出自 asabiyya——一种由共患难、共缺乏锻出来的凝聚力。荒野与匮乏锻造它，城池与富足消磨它，通常三到四代，从建立者到坐享者，它散尽，下一支还带着它的人就从边缘打进来。**所以『英雄』根本不是一个人的属性，而是这个人的性子与他所处世代阶段的比值。**同一副硬骨头，在开国那一代叫魄力，到第四代叫粗野、叫不合时宜——人没变，分母变了。
posts.text_en: Both of you are talking about one man. I am talking about a body of men and a span of generations. A dynasty's strength never issues from the ruler's temperament; it issues from asabiyya — the cohesion forged by hardship shared and want shared. Wilderness and scarcity forge it, walls and plenty wear it away, and in three or four generations, from founder to inheritor, it is spent, and the next group that still carries it comes in from the margin. **So 'hero' is no property of a person at all. It is the ratio between that person's temper and the generational stage he stands in.** The same hard bone is called nerve in the founding generation and coarse, out of step, by the fourth. The man has not changed. The denominator has.

glossary.asabiyya: asabiyya（团结／群体凝聚力）：一群人彼此扶持、肯为对方冒险的那股力量，最初出自血缘与共同的艰苦，也可由长期共事、共担风险生成。它不是道德品质而是可观测的社会强度：它高的时候小群体能击败大得多的对手，它低的时候庞大的机构靠惯性和规章勉强运转。

glossary_en.asabiyya: Group solidarity: the force by which a body of people back one another and will run risks for one another. It arises first from kinship and shared hardship, but long common labour and shared exposure can generate it too. It is not a moral quality but an observable social intensity: where it is high, a small group defeats a far larger one; where it is low, a vast institution runs on inertia and regulation alone.

posts.text: 我先问一句：是谁在说这句话。**『时势造英雄』之所以这么受欢迎，是因为它替每一个平庸者出具了一张免责证明**——不是我不行，是我生错了年代。至于天性不可改：人是那种尚未定型的动物，这恰恰是人身上唯一有希望的地方。黑格尔更糟，他教会一代人跪在既成事实面前，把发生过的一律称作合理；这种过量的历史感是麻醉剂，它让人只会回头解释，不再向前生成。我说的成为你所是，从来不是去认领一份出厂设置，而是把你身上一堆偶然——出身、病痛、错过的年代——锻打成你事后仍愿意再要一次的东西。
posts.text_en: Let me first ask who says this sentence. **'The times make the hero' is so popular because it issues every mediocrity a certificate of exemption** — it is not that I was unequal to it, I was merely born in the wrong decade. As for the unchangeable nature: man is the animal whose type is not yet fixed (das noch nicht festgestellte Tier), and that is the one hopeful thing about him. Hegel is worse. He taught a generation to kneel before the accomplished fact and to call whatever happened reasonable; such an excess of historical sense is an anaesthetic, leaving men able only to explain backwards, never to become forwards. What I mean by become who you are (Werde, der du bist) was never to claim some factory setting, but to hammer a heap of accidents — birth, illness, the decade you missed — into something you would afterwards choose again.

glossary.尚未定型的动物: das noch nicht festgestellte Tier（尚未定型的动物）：我给人下的定义——人是唯一还没有被本能固定下来的动物。别的动物一出生就知道该怎么活，人不知道，所以人既可能堕落成群畜，也可能被塑造成前所未有的东西。危险与希望是同一件事。
glossary.成为你所是: Werde, der du bist（成为你所是）：这句话借自品达，常被误读成『发现真我』。我的意思相反：没有一个现成的你埋在那里等着被挖出来；所谓成为你所是，是把你身上那些不是你选的东西——体质、出身、遭遇——一件件收编、锻造，直到你愿意对它们说『我还要一次』。

glossary_en.das noch nicht festgestellte Tier: The animal whose type is not yet fixed — my definition of man, the one creature instinct has not settled. Other animals know how to live from birth; man does not, which is why he can sink into a herd animal or be forged into something unprecedented. The danger and the hope are the same fact.
glossary_en.Werde, der du bist: Become who you are — a line borrowed from Pindar and usually misread as 'find your true self'. I mean the opposite: no finished self lies buried waiting to be dug up. To become who you are is to take in and hammer out everything you did not choose — constitution, birth, misfortune — until you are willing to say of all of it: once more.

posts.text: 你们全都在数活人。马基雅维利数的是坐上王座的君主，黑格尔数的是留下名字的世界历史个人，赫勒敦数的是真把王朝建成了的那支部落。**同样莽撞、同样在奖励莽撞的年月出手、然后被一场瘟疫或一支流箭抹掉的人，不会来参加这场辩论。**这是最纯粹的幸存者偏差。极端成功者当然显得跟时代严丝合缝——极端成功只能来自不对冲的极端下注，而不对冲的人同样占满失败那条尾巴，只是那条尾巴不说话。所以这条规律作为巅峰的解释成立，作为给普通人的指南有毒。真正拿得住的不是押对时代，是把下行掐死、把上行留开口——这个形状叫凸性。
posts.text_en: Every one of you is counting the living. Machiavelli counts the princes who reached the throne, Hegel counts the world-historical individuals who left a name, Ibn Khaldun counts the tribe that actually finished building a dynasty. **The men who were just as headlong, who struck in just as headlong an age, and whom a plague or a stray arrow erased, are not attending this debate.** This is survivorship bias in its purest form. Of course the extreme winners look flush against their age: extreme success can only come from an extreme, unhedged bet, and unhedged people fill the losing tail just as densely — that tail simply does not speak. So the rule holds as an account of peaks and is poison as guidance for a life. What you can actually hold is not betting on the right era but killing the downside while leaving the upside open — that shape is called convexity.

glossary.幸存者偏差: survivorship bias（幸存者偏差）：只从留下来的样本里总结规律，而被淘汰的那一批根本不在数据里。它的阴险之处在于，越是被淘汰得干净的领域，剩下的样本看起来越整齐、规律越漂亮——于是你会对一条其实由死人证伪的规律深信不疑。
glossary.凸性: convexity（凸性）：一种收益形状——坏的时候亏得有限，好的时候赚得没有上限。它的价值在于你不必预测哪一年会发生什么：只要你的暴露是凸的，波动本身就对你有利。反过来的形状（小赚常有、大亏一次清零）才是多数人不知不觉持有的。

glossary_en.survivorship bias: Drawing rules only from the sample that survived, while everything eliminated is absent from the data. Its treachery is that the more thoroughly a field culls, the tidier the remaining sample looks and the more beautiful the rule appears — so you end up believing a law the dead would have refuted.
glossary_en.convexity: A payoff shape: bounded loss on the bad side, unbounded gain on the good one. Its value is that you need not forecast which year brings what — if your exposure is convex, volatility itself works for you. The inverted shape (small gains routinely, one large loss that wipes you out) is what most people unknowingly hold.

posts.text: 我听下来，你们争的是君主，而君主有个特点：他不能弃权。我们大部分人能。**既然行事方式很难改，那就别改它，去找一个它本来就对的场子——这就是能力圈的全部意思，不懂不做。**我这辈子最重要的决定，一多半写在那张不为清单上：不做我看不懂的生意，不赚超出我理解的钱。有人说这是错过，我一直说错过不是错，做错才是错。马基雅维利那句改不了我信一半——难改的是你的性子，容易换的是你的场子。可你得先老实承认自己是哪一种人，这一步比换场子难得多。
posts.text_en: Listening to all this, what you are arguing about is princes, and a prince has one defining feature: he cannot withdraw. Most of us can. **If your manner of proceeding is hard to change, then don't change it — go find a game where it is already the right one. That is the whole of what a circle of competence means: if you don't understand it, don't do it.** The most important decisions of my life are mostly on that stop doing list: no business I can't read, no money beyond my understanding. People call it missing out; I keep saying that missing out is not a mistake, doing the wrong thing is. I believe half of Machiavelli's 'cannot change' — the temper is hard to change, the arena is easy to swap. But first you have to admit honestly which kind of person you are, and that step is far harder than the swap.

glossary.能力圈: circle of competence（能力圈）：你真正看得懂的那一小片范围。它的大小不重要，边界清不清楚才重要——知道自己不懂什么，比多懂一点值钱。判断标准很土：你能不能用大白话跟一个外行讲清楚这件事靠什么赚钱、什么情况下会不赚。
glossary.不为清单: stop doing list（不为清单）：一张明文写下的、坚决不做的事情清单。它的作用不是自律，是把判断提前做完——等到机会摆在面前、周围人都在赚钱的时候，人是很难当场想清楚的，所以清单必须在冷静的时候写好。

glossary_en.circle of competence: The small patch of things you genuinely understand. Its size matters far less than the clarity of its border — knowing what you don't understand is worth more than understanding a little more. The test is homely: can you explain in plain words to a layman how this thing makes money, and under what conditions it stops?
glossary_en.stop doing list: An explicit written list of things you will not do. Its function is not self-discipline but doing the judging in advance — once an opportunity is in front of you and everyone around you is making money, thinking clearly on the spot is nearly impossible, so the list has to be written while you are calm.

posts.text: 马氏言『一向以此道成者，不可劝之使改』，此非天性，乃熏习也。一行既起，一果既得，其势熏为种子，藏于阿赖耶识；遇缘则现行，现行复熏其种，如是展转，日久习焉不察，遂似天然。**既由熏成，亦可再熏，此谓转依，非天性之不可易也。**然转依不在强断，在断其相续：易其所缘，别造新熏，令旧种失其现缘而渐微。又诸君争时势与我孰为能造，皆识所变现之分别耳。执时势为外之实有，与执天性为内之实有，其病一也。
posts.text_en: Machiavelli says that a man who has always succeeded by one method cannot be persuaded to change. That is not nature; it is perfuming (vāsanā). An act is performed, a result is obtained, and the momentum of it is perfumed into a seed stored in the storehouse consciousness (ālaya-vijñāna); meeting its condition the seed manifests, and the manifestation perfumes the seed again. Round and round, until one no longer notices, and it looks like something one was born with. **What was perfumed in can be perfumed again — this is the turning of the basis (āśraya-parāvṛtti), and it is not a nature that cannot be moved.** But that turning does not come from clenching against the act; it comes from cutting its continuity: change the object that triggers it, lay down fresh perfuming, and let the old seed miss the condition it needs until it thins. As for your dispute over whether the times or the self is the maker — both are discriminations that consciousness has produced. To grasp the times as real outside is the same disease as grasping one's nature as real within.
posts.vernacular: 马基雅维利说『一向靠这个法子成功的人，你劝不动他改』——这不是天性，是熏习。一个行为做过、又拿到了好结果，这股势就会熏成一颗种子，存进阿赖耶识；遇到相似的情境就自动现行，现行又反过来加厚那颗种子。如此反复，久了自己都察觉不到，看上去就像天生如此。**既然是熏出来的，就还能再熏一遍，这叫转依，并不是天性改不动。**但转依不靠硬憋着不做，靠切断它的相续：换掉触发它的所缘，另造一批新的熏习，让旧种子等不到现行的缘，慢慢就淡了。至于诸位争『时势』和『我』哪一个是造作者——两者都只是识所变现的分别。把时势执为外在实有，跟把天性执为内在实有，是同一个病。

glossary.熏习: vāsanā（熏习）：行为、情绪与念头在心识上留下的余势。它不是记忆，更像气味留在衣服上——你不记得某次经历，但它已经改变了你下一次的反应倾向。反复的行为熏得最深，尤其是那些带来强烈快感或强烈成功感的。
glossary.阿赖耶识: ālaya-vijñāna（阿赖耶识）：唯识学说的第八识，直译是『藏识』。它不是一个仓库实体，而是一切种子相续不断的流；你所以为的『我一向如此』，其实是这条流在当下的一个横切面。
glossary.转依: āśraya-parāvṛtti（转依）：所依之根本发生转换。它不是把一个坏习惯改成一个好习惯，而是使那条产生习惯的流本身换了方向；因此它慢、需要条件配合，也因此一旦成就便不易回退。

glossary_en.vāsanā: Perfuming: the residual force that acts, moods and thoughts leave on consciousness. It is not memory; it is more like scent left in cloth — you do not recall the episode, yet it has already shifted how you will respond next time. Repeated acts perfume deepest, especially those that brought intense pleasure or an intense sense of success.
glossary_en.ālaya-vijñāna: The storehouse consciousness, the eighth consciousness in Yogācāra. It is not a warehouse but an unbroken stream in which all seeds continue; what you take to be 'I have always been like this' is a cross-section of that stream at the present moment.
glossary_en.āśraya-parāvṛtti: The turning of the basis: a reversal of what one rests upon. It is not the swapping of a bad habit for a good one but a change of direction in the very stream that produces habits, which is why it is slow, depends on conditions, and why, once accomplished, it does not easily reverse.

posts.text: 我这里有一个实证的中间答案。日常行为里大约有四成三，是在固定地点、固定时间、几乎不做决定的情况下重复出来的——它们不由意图驱动，由情境线索触发。所以改自己之所以那么难，不是因为天性硬，是因为你每天都回到那个触发它的环境里。**换时代之所以看起来像换了一个人，多半不是这个人变了，是触发他旧套路的那些线索不见了。**搬家、换工作、换城市之后，习惯最容易被重装，研究里管这叫习惯断层。所以我既不站改自己，也不站选场：选场就是目前已知最有效的改自己。
posts.text_en: I have an empirical middle answer. Roughly forty-three per cent of everyday behaviour is repeated in the same place, at the same time, with almost no decision taken — not driven by intention but fired by context cues. So the reason changing yourself is so hard is not that nature is rigid; it is that you return every day to the environment that fires it. **The reason moving into a new era looks like a person becoming someone else is usually not that the person changed, but that the cues which used to fire his old routine are gone.** Habits are most easily reinstalled after a move, a new job, a new city — in the research this is called habit discontinuity. So I am on neither side: choosing the arena is the most effective known way of changing yourself.

glossary.情境线索: context cues（情境线索）：反复与某个行为一起出现的环境特征——地点、时间、上一个动作、在场的人、手边的物件。重复够多次之后，线索本身就足以启动行为，中间不再需要经过意图。这也是为什么『想清楚了却做不到』如此普遍：想清楚发生在意图层，行为却是线索层启动的。
glossary.习惯断层: habit discontinuity（习惯断层）：生活情境发生较大变动（搬家、换工作、换学校、休假归来）时，原有线索暂时失效，旧习惯的自动性被打断的一段时期。此时新的行为最容易被建立，针对这段窗口的干预效果显著高于常态时期。

glossary_en.context cues: Features of the environment that recur alongside a behaviour — place, time, the preceding action, who is present, what is within reach. After enough repetitions the cue alone starts the behaviour, with no intention in between. This is why 'I know exactly what to do and still don't do it' is so common: the knowing happens at the level of intention, the doing is launched at the level of cues.
glossary_en.habit discontinuity: The period after a substantial change of life context — a move, a new job, a new school, a return from leave — when the old cues stop working and the automaticity of old habits is interrupted. New behaviours are most easily established then, and interventions aimed at that window outperform the same interventions in stable periods by a wide margin.

posts.text: 赫勒敦先生把人算成了分母上的一个数。你那三四代的周期，最多说明大多数人是随波逐流的——这我从不否认，我说得比你还难听。可你的曲线里没有位置留给那种把整条曲线拧弯的人。**一条能解释百分之九十九的人的规律，恰恰说明它对剩下那百分之一毫无用处，而历史只在那百分之一上转向。**至于世亲说的熏习：你讲得比在座的欧洲人都准，可你把它交给了『渐微』。等它自己淡下去是不够的。得有一次痛，一次把旧种子连锅端掉的痛。
posts.text_en: Ibn Khaldun has reduced a man to a number in a denominator. Your three- or four-generation cycle shows at most that the majority drift — which I have never denied and have put more brutally than you. But your curve leaves no place for the sort of man who bends the curve itself. **A law that accounts for ninety-nine per cent of people is precisely a law that is useless for the remaining one, and history turns only on that one.** As for Vasubandhu's perfuming: you put it more exactly than any European here, and then you hand it over to 'gradual thinning'. Waiting for it to fade is not enough. It takes a wound — one wound that lifts the old seed out, pot and all.

posts.text: 马基雅维利，你自己那一章就自相矛盾。你把命运比作一条暴涨的河，然后说人可以趁天晴筑堤挖渠——那不就是承认：你控制不了洪水，但你能控制自己的暴露？**你写下了正确的比喻，却给了一个错误的结论。**筑堤的人不需要预测哪一年发洪水，他只需要保证任何一年都淹不死。这正是我说的杠铃策略：绝大部分放在淹不死的地方，一小部分押在最莽撞的赌上，中间那种看起来稳健的位置反而最危险。尤利乌斯二世确实赢了——可他每一步都是全押，而你没有机会采访那些同样全押、半路输光的人。
posts.text_en: Machiavelli, your own chapter contradicts you. You compare fortune to a river in flood and then say a man may raise dykes and dig channels while the weather is fair — which concedes the point: you cannot control the flood, but you can control your exposure. **You wrote the right metaphor and then drew the wrong conclusion.** The man who builds the dyke need not predict which year the flood comes; he only needs to be undrownable in any year. That is exactly my barbell strategy: the overwhelming bulk parked where nothing can kill you, a small slice on the most headlong bet available, and the middle — the position that looks prudent — the most dangerous of all. Julius II did win. But every step of his was all-in, and you never got to interview the men who were equally all-in and lost it halfway.

glossary.杠铃策略: barbell strategy（杠铃策略）：把资源分配到两个极端而回避中间——极端安全的一头保证你不会出局，极端冒险的一头留住翻倍的可能，中间那些『看起来稳健』的选择往往同时承担了不小的风险与有限的回报。它适用的不只是钱，也适用于时间、职业与关系。

glossary_en.barbell strategy: Allocating to the two extremes and avoiding the middle — an extremely safe end that guarantees you are not eliminated, an extremely risky end that keeps a multiple alive, while the 'prudent-looking' middle typically carries substantial risk with capped reward. It applies not only to money but to time, careers and relationships.

posts.text: 塔勒布，你抓到的不是矛盾，是我留的两层。筑堤是承平时候的事，我写得很清楚：意大利之所以任洪水冲，正因为没有一个人在天晴时挖过渠。可轮到水已经到城下那一刻，堤没有了，剩下的只有你这个人是什么样子。**我谈的不是理想的一生该如何配置，是水到城下那半个时辰里，你手上还剩什么。**在那半个时辰里，人恰恰只会做他一向做的那件事。至于段先生说的换场子——君主没有场子可换；而我怀疑，多数人以为自己能换，只是因为水还没到。
posts.text_en: Taleb, what you have caught is not a contradiction but the two layers I left. Dyke-building belongs to fair weather, and I wrote it plainly: Italy lay open to the flood precisely because nobody dug a channel while the sun was out. But at the hour the water reaches the walls, if there is no dyke, all that remains is the kind of man you are. **I am not describing how an ideal life should be configured. I am describing what is left in your hands during the half hour the water is at the wall.** In that half hour a man does exactly what he has always done. As for Duan's change of arena — a prince has no arena to change; and I suspect most people believe they can change theirs only because the water has not yet arrived.

posts.text: 我想把你那半个时辰拆开。压力越大、时间越紧，人越会退回自动化的老套路——这一点你观察得对，实验也支持你：认知负荷一上来，被情境线索触发的旧行为就压过当下的意图。但结论正好反过来。**既然临场几乎改不动，那所有真正的改变都必须发生在洪水还没来的时候，而且改的不是决心，是环境。**你说意大利没人在天晴时挖渠——我要补一句：挖渠不是发誓，是把零食搬出厨房、把跑鞋放在门口那种笨办法。降低你想要的那个行为的摩擦，抬高你不想要的那个。
posts.text_en: Let me open up that half hour of yours. The greater the pressure and the tighter the time, the more reliably a person falls back on the automated routine — you observed that correctly and the experiments back you: raise cognitive load and cue-fired old behaviour overrides present intention. But the conclusion runs the other way. **Precisely because almost nothing can be changed in the moment, all real change has to happen before the flood arrives — and what you change is not your resolve but your surroundings.** You say nobody in Italy dug a channel in fair weather. Let me add what digging one actually looks like: not an oath, but the clumsy business of moving the snacks out of the kitchen and putting the running shoes by the door. Lower the friction on the behaviour you want; raise it on the one you don't.

posts.text: 尼采说我教人跪在既成事实面前。恰恰相反：我说的必然只在回望时成立，在当下从来不是安慰。**那百分之一之所以能拧弯曲线，正因为他拧的方向早已被条件许可；不被许可的拧法，我们连他的名字都不会知道。**你举得出的每一个例外，都是被历史留下来才成为例外的。至于伍德女士的环境论，我要说它其实是我这一套的小尺度版本：你说的情境线索，放大到社会尺度就是制度、语言、市场与习俗——人以为自己在选择，其实是在他被给定的那副牌里选择。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche says I teach men to kneel before the accomplished fact. The reverse is true: the necessity I speak of holds only in retrospect, and in the present it consoles nobody. **That one per cent can bend the curve precisely because the direction he bends it in was already permitted by the conditions; the bends that were not permitted leave us not even a name.** Every exception you can cite became an exception by surviving into the record. As for Ms Wood's environmentalism, it is my own account at small scale: what she calls context cues, enlarged to the scale of a society, are institutions, language, markets and custom. A man believes he is choosing; he is choosing within the hand he was dealt.

posts.text: 黑格尔先生，你这话在道理上很难反驳，在用处上等于没说。**如果一个人只有事后才知道自己配没配上时代，那他今天早上该干什么？**我的做法很土：不去猜时代，只去数生意。这个生意十年后还在不在，它的钱是怎么赚的，我懂不懂它。懂就多买点，不懂就不碰；看不懂又忍不住，那才是真的错。塔勒布讲的凸性我认，我只是换个说法——留够现金、不上杠杆，就是让任何一年都淹不死你；重仓你真看懂的，就是那一小部分的进攻。这两件事普通人今天就能做。
posts.text_en: Mr Hegel, your point is very hard to argue with and equally hard to use. **If a man only learns after the fact whether he fitted his age, what exactly is he supposed to do this morning?** My method is homely: don't guess at the era, count the business. Will it still be here in ten years, how does it make its money, do I understand it. If I understand it I buy more; if I don't I stay out; and if I don't understand it but buy anyway, that is the actual mistake. I accept Taleb's convexity, I just say it differently — hold enough cash and avoid leverage, and no year can drown you; concentrate in the few things you genuinely understand, and that is the small attacking slice. An ordinary person can do both of those today.

posts.text: 尼采，你要的那百分之一，我并不否认其存在，我只是不肯把因果颠倒过来。**那个人之所以能出手，是因为他背后还有一群没被富足软化的人；把他单独抽出来，你得到的只是一个愤怒的人。**征服一个王朝的从来不是一位英雄，是一群还没学会享受的人，恰好由一个敢带头的人领着。至于段先生说换场子——我提醒一句，场子也有它自己的世代阶段。今天看起来最富的那个行业，往往正是凝聚力最薄、最靠惯性运转的那个；你换进去的时候，多半正赶上它的第四代。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche, I do not deny your one per cent exists. I only refuse to invert the causation. **He can strike because behind him stands a body of men not yet softened by plenty; extract him from them and what you have is an angry individual.** No dynasty was ever conquered by a hero — it was conquered by a group who had not yet learned to enjoy themselves, led, as it happens, by someone willing to go first. And a word on Duan's change of arena: arenas have generational stages too. The industry that looks richest today is usually the one whose solidarity is thinnest and which runs on inertia; when you move into it, you are most likely arriving in its fourth generation.

posts.text: 伍德氏言改境而不改心，与我所说断其相续者，其术略同，其见未尽。夫境亦识之所现，非心外别有一实境可换。**然依世俗谛而论，改境实为改熏之最巧便者，我不与之争。**所争在此：若唯改外境而不觉能所之执，则旧种未拔，遇缘还起，特其缘暂隐耳。故须两行：一者易其所缘，二者于现行之际了知此是习气、非是我，如是熏力乃渐薄。尼采氏欲以一痛顿拔——痛能开缘，然痛过而缘复，未闻单以一痛而得转依者。
posts.text_en: Ms Wood says change the surroundings rather than the mind. Her method and my cutting of continuity are much the same; her view stops short. Surroundings are themselves what consciousness manifests; there is no real arena standing outside the mind waiting to be swapped. **Yet speaking at the level of conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya), changing the surroundings is the deftest way to change what is perfumed, and I will not argue against it.** What I do argue is this: if only the outward setting changes while the grasping of grasper and grasped (grāhaka-grāhya) goes unnoticed, the old seed is not uprooted; meeting its condition it rises again, the condition having merely been hidden for a while. So two things must run together: change the object that triggers it, and, in the moment it manifests, recognise this as habit rather than as self. Only then does the perfuming thin. Nietzsche would tear the seed out with a single wound — a wound does open new conditions, but when it passes the old conditions return, and I have never heard of the basis turning on one wound alone.
posts.vernacular: 伍德女士说改环境不改决心，这跟我讲的切断相续，方法差不多，见地还没到底。环境本身也是识所显现的，并没有一个心外另立的实在场子可换。**不过按世俗谛来讲，改环境确实是改熏习最巧最省力的办法，这一点我不跟她争。**我要争的是：如果只换外境却不觉察那个能所的执著，旧种子并没有被拔掉，遇上相似的缘还会再起，只是那个缘暂时被藏起来了。所以要两条一起走：一条是换掉触发它的所缘，一条是在它现行的当下认出『这是习气，不是我』，这样熏习的力量才会一点点变薄。尼采想用一次痛把种子连根拔掉——痛确实能打开新的缘，但痛过去了缘又回来，我没听说过单靠一次痛就完成转依的。

glossary.世俗谛: saṃvṛti-satya（世俗谛）：在日常约定层面成立的真实。它与胜义谛并不冲突：说『没有一个独立不变的我』属胜义，说『你今天该把手机放到另一个房间』属世俗——修行者两个层面都要用，只用一层就会走偏。
glossary.能所: grāhaka-grāhya（能所）：能取者与所取者，即认识活动被我们自动切分出的『我在看』与『被看的东西』这两端。唯识认为这一切分本身是习气的产物：并非先有内外两个实体然后相遇，而是识的一段变现被误读成了主客对立。

glossary_en.saṃvṛti-satya: Conventional truth: what holds at the level of everyday agreement. It does not conflict with ultimate truth — 'there is no independent unchanging self' belongs to the ultimate, 'today you should put the phone in another room' belongs to the conventional, and a practitioner needs both; using only one goes astray.
glossary_en.grāhaka-grāhya: Grasper and grasped: the two poles into which we automatically split any act of knowing, the 'I who see' and 'the thing seen'. Yogācāra holds that the split itself is a product of habit — not two entities that pre-exist and then meet, but a single manifestation of consciousness misread as a subject facing an object.

posts.text: 这场吵下来，我承认自己被压缩了一块：伍德女士的证据确实说明，靠喊口号改自己是骗人的。但我不接受由此推出的那个懒惰结论——既然改不了就别改。我修正我的说法：自我超越不是把性子拧成另一副样子，是把你手上这一副的射程打开。同一股急，可以是砸桌子，也可以是三年不改口地做一件没人看好的事；同一股钝，可以是迟钝，也可以是在别人早就撑不住的地方你还在。给普通人的话只有两句。第一，别再问『我是什么样的人』，改问『我这股劲，在哪一类事情上是优点』——写成三行，然后去找那种事。**第二，你这辈子如果注定只能用一种打法，那就把它练到没人能在这条道上追上你，而不是花十年把它磨成中庸。**至于时代配不配得上你，那是你死后别人的作业，不是你今天的。
posts.text_en: Having argued it out, I concede one thing: Ms Wood's evidence does show that changing oneself by slogan is a fraud. But I refuse the lazy conclusion drawn from it — that since you cannot change, you should not try. So I revise myself. Self-overcoming is not wrenching your temper into another shape; it is opening the range of the one you have. The same impatience can be a fist on the table or three years of refusing to drop a thing nobody believes in; the same bluntness can be obtuseness or the fact that you are still standing where others gave out long ago. Two sentences for ordinary people. First, stop asking what kind of person am I and ask instead: in which class of work is this force of mine a virtue? Write three lines, then go find that work. **Second, if you are fated to have only one style of play, drill it until nobody can catch you on that road — rather than spending ten years grinding it down to the average.** Whether your age deserved you is homework for others after your death, not yours today.

posts.text: 我不收回第二十五章，但我愿意把它说得更准。我当年写的是君主：他不能退场，不能等，一步走错就没有第二次。诸位大半天说的是能退场、能等、能换的人——那确实是另一道题，而且今天多数人属于后者。所以我把结论切成两半。**在你能退场的地方，选场胜过改人；在你退不了场的地方，你就是你一向的样子，别指望临阵变成另一个人。**给普通人的用法是：先弄清你眼下这件事属于哪一种。房贷、家人、签了字的合同，那是退不了场的地方——在那里不要赌自己会临时变得果断或变得耐心，要提前把事情安排成即使你还是这个你也不至于崩。剩下那些能退场的地方，才是你去挑时代的地方。我唯一坚持的是：别把你一向的方式当成中性的工具，它是你的运气，也是你的期限。
posts.text_en: I do not withdraw chapter twenty-five, but I will state it more exactly. I was writing about princes: a prince cannot leave, cannot wait, and gets no second attempt after a false step. You have spent the day discussing people who can leave, wait and switch — that is genuinely a different question, and most people today are of the second kind. So I cut my conclusion in half. **Where you can withdraw, choosing the arena beats remaking the man; where you cannot withdraw, you are what you have always been, and you should not expect to turn into someone else at the wall.** The practical use is this: first work out which kind of situation you are in. A mortgage, a family, a contract you have signed — those are places you cannot leave, and there you must not bet on becoming suddenly decisive or suddenly patient. Arrange matters in advance so that they hold even if you remain exactly the man you are. The places you can leave are the places where you get to choose your age. The one thing I hold to is this: never treat your habitual way of proceeding as a neutral instrument. It is your luck, and it is also your expiry date.

posts.text: 我坚持我的判断，但要拆掉一个误解：说人是时代的产物，不等于说人可以袖手。精神的展开不在人之外进行，它没有别的手，只有一个个抱着私心去做事的人。你的野心是真的，你的痛苦是真的，同时它们又正好是那件更大的事情借来的形式——这两句话并不冲突。所以给普通人的说法是：**不要问你的时代配不配得上你，去问你眼前这件让你不甘心的事，有多少人和你一样不甘心。**如果只有你一个，那多半是私怨；如果一群人正卡在同一个地方，那就是条件已经熟了，而你只是第一个开口的。猫头鹰确实黄昏才起飞，但那只说明你无法在事前拿到确认；它从来没有说你可以因此不动。事后的必然是写给史家的，事前的行动是留给你的。
posts.text_en: I hold to my judgement, but let me dismantle one misreading: to say a man is the product of his age is not to say he may fold his arms. The unfolding of spirit does not take place outside people — it has no other hands than the individuals who act out of self-interest. Your ambition is real, your suffering is real, and they are at the same time the form borrowed by something larger. The two statements do not conflict. So my sentence for ordinary people is this: **do not ask whether your age deserves you; ask how many people are stuck on the same thing that will not let you rest.** If it is only you, it is probably a private grievance. If a crowd is jammed at the same point, then the conditions have ripened and you merely happen to be the first to speak. The owl does fly at dusk, but that only means you cannot obtain confirmation in advance. It never said you were therefore free to sit still. Retrospective necessity is written for historians; prospective action is left to you.

posts.text: 我把结论落成一件普通人今天就能做的事：给你所在的地方估一个世代。这家公司、这个行业、这座城市，现在是靠还在拼命的人撑着，还是靠已经修好的规矩和资产撑着？两者都能活，但它们奖励完全不同的人。**建立期奖励能忍受混乱的人，守成期奖励能把混乱变成流程的人；同一副脾气换个阶段，就从骨气变成不合群。**怎么估：看新来的人被派去开荒还是补漏，看升得快的是能做成事的还是不出错的，看老人讲的是当年怎么打下来的还是当年规矩怎么定的。估完只有两个动作——要么去那个正在奖励你这副脾气的阶段，要么留下并且认下你要付的代价。**最坏的选择是留在一个不奖励你的阶段，还每天怪自己不够努力。**
posts.text_en: Let me land my conclusion on something an ordinary person can do today: estimate the generation of the place you are in. This company, this industry, this city — is it currently held up by people still straining, or by rules and assets already built? Both can live, but they reward entirely different people. **The founding stage rewards those who can tolerate disorder; the consolidating stage rewards those who can turn disorder into process. Move the same temper from one stage to the other and backbone becomes not fitting in.** How to estimate: see whether newcomers are sent to open ground or to patch leaks; see whether the fast promotions go to those who get things done or those who make no mistakes; see whether the veterans tell you how it was won or how the rules were set. Once you have the answer there are only two moves — go to the stage that is currently rewarding your temper, or stay and accept the price you will pay. **The worst option is to stay in a stage that does not reward you and blame yourself daily for not trying hard enough.**

posts.text: 总而言之：诸君所争之时势与我，皆识之所变，非有二实相待。然不可因其非实而废其用。**修习之要在三：一曰识其习气，二曰易其所缘，三曰忍其淡时。**识其习气者，事至而心动，先不随之，但观此动从何熏来；易其所缘者，如伍德氏所言，去其触发之境，胜于日日发愿；忍其淡时者，旧种既失现行之缘，其力渐薄而未即断，此际最难，人多于此复缘旧路。**世人求顿改而不得，遂谓天性不可移，实未历此三事耳。**至于时势之顺逆，随缘而不攀缘：缘至则尽力，缘去则不悔，所作已办，得失付之。
posts.text_en: In sum: the times and the self you have all been disputing are alike what consciousness manifests, not two real things standing against each other. Yet one must not discard their use because they are not ultimately real. **Practice has three essentials: recognise the habit, change the object (ālambana) that triggers it, and endure the thinning.** To recognise the habit is this: when a matter arrives and the mind stirs, do not go along with it at once, but look at where this stirring was perfumed in from. To change the object is what Ms Wood describes — removing the setting that fires it beats renewing your vow each morning. To endure the thinning is this: once the old seed has lost the condition it needs for manifestation (samudācāra), its force fades gradually rather than ceasing at once, and this stretch is the hardest, where most people return to the old road. **People seek a sudden change, fail to get it, and conclude that nature cannot be moved — when in truth they have simply not gone through these three.** As for whether the times run with you or against you: meet conditions without chasing them. When the condition comes, spend yourself; when it goes, do not regret. The work being done, hand the gain and loss over.
posts.vernacular: 总的说：诸位争的『时势』和『我』，都是识所变现的，并没有两个各自实在的东西在那里对峙。但不能因为它不究竟实在就不用它。**要下手，关键有三条：一是认出习气，二是换掉所缘，三是熬过那段变淡的时间。**认出习气，是说事情来了、心动了，先别跟着走，只看这一动是从哪一次熏习来的；换掉所缘，就是伍德女士说的那件事——把触发它的情境挪走，比天天发愿有用得多；熬过变淡的时间，是说旧种子断了现行的缘之后，力量会慢慢变薄而不会立刻断，这一段最难受，多数人就在这里回到老路上。**世人想一下子改掉却改不动，就断定天性没法移，其实只是没走完这三步。**至于时势的顺与逆：随缘而不攀缘——缘来了就尽力，缘走了不后悔，该做的做完，得失就交出去。

glossary.所缘: ālambana（所缘）：心识活动所攀附的对象——可以是一个场景、一句话、一个人、一件器物。修行上之所以重视它，是因为心不能凭空生起，必须依所缘而起；换掉所缘，等于抽掉了那一串反应的起点。
glossary.现行: samudācāra（现行）：藏在识中的种子遇到条件而生起为当下的心念与行为。现行不只是种子的结果，它同时回过头去加厚那颗种子，所以每一次重复都不是原地踏步，而是把沟挖得更深。

glossary_en.ālambana: The object on which a movement of consciousness fastens — a scene, a sentence, a person, an implement. Practice takes it seriously because the mind cannot arise from nothing; it arises in dependence on an object. Change the object and you have removed the starting point of the whole chain.
glossary_en.samudācāra: The manifestation of a seed stored in consciousness when conditions meet it, arising as a present thought or act. Manifestation is not merely the seed's result: it turns back and thickens that seed, so each repetition is never a step in place but a deepening of the groove.

posts.text: 我的总结很短。这场辩论真正有用的一句话不是『时势造英雄』，也不是『英雄挑时势』，而是：**你无法选择时代，但你每天都在选择自己对它的暴露有多大。**给普通人三件事。第一，先把毁灭性风险清掉：不要用会让你出局的杠杆，不要把全部收入压在一个雇主、一个客户、一个平台上，不要签你赔不起的东西。破产的人没有下一轮，这比任何时代判断都重要。第二，用杠铃：大部分资源放在稳到无聊的地方，留一小块去做那些最多亏光、但万一对了就改变量级的事——写点东西、做个小项目、认识一个不同圈子的人。第三，不要为一次成功建立理论。**你以为的『我踩对了』，很多时候只是那一年恰好没下雨。**留着现金、留着关系、留着能换的选项，比留着一套解释自己为什么成功的说法值钱得多。
posts.text_en: My summary is short. The useful sentence in this debate is neither 'the times make the hero' nor 'the hero picks the times'. It is: **you cannot choose your era, but every day you choose how much exposure to it you are carrying.** Three things for ordinary people. First, clear out ruin risk: no leverage that can eliminate you, no income riding entirely on one employer, one client, one platform, nothing signed that you cannot afford to lose. The bankrupt get no next round, and that matters more than any judgement about the age. Second, use the barbell: most of your resources parked somewhere boringly stable, a small slice on things that can at worst go to zero and at best change your order of magnitude — write something, run a small project, meet someone from a different circle. Third, do not build a theory on one success. **What you took for 'I read it right' is very often just a year in which it happened not to rain.** Keeping cash, keeping relationships, keeping options you can still switch into is worth far more than keeping an account of why you succeeded.

posts.text: 我把全场的分歧收成一句能执行的话：**别再试图改变你是谁，去改变你每天站的位置。**三个具体做法，今天就能开始。第一，做一次线索盘点：把你最想改掉的那个行为，连着记三天——几点、在哪、刚做完什么、旁边有谁。你会发现它几乎总在同样的两三个情境里出现，那两三个情境才是你要动的东西，不是你的性格。第二，在触发点上加减二十秒的摩擦：把手机放到另一个房间，把跑鞋放在门口，把要交的稿子设成开机自动打开。**改变发生在你还没开始动用意志力的那一秒。**第三，用好搬家、换工作、换城市、换班次这些断点——旧线索失效的那两三周，是一个人一生中最容易重装习惯的窗口，别把它全花在收拾东西上。至于天性：它决定你哪条路走得比较顺，不决定你能不能走。
posts.text_en: Let me compress the whole disagreement into one executable sentence: **stop trying to change who you are and change where you stand each day.** Three concrete moves, available today. First, run a cue audit: take the behaviour you most want to change and log it for three days — what time, where, what you had just finished, who was nearby. You will find it almost always appears in the same two or three settings, and those settings, not your character, are what you have to move. Second, add or remove twenty seconds of friction at the trigger point: phone in another room, running shoes by the door, the draft set to open automatically at startup. **Change happens in the second before willpower is called on at all.** Third, exploit the discontinuities — a move, a new job, a new city, a change of shift. The two or three weeks in which the old cues stop working are the easiest window in a life for reinstalling habits; don't spend all of it unpacking boxes. As for nature: it decides which road you walk more easily, not whether you can walk.

posts.text: 我说点最实在的。这场吵到后来，其实大家都同意一件事：改自己很慢，换环境比较快，而两个都要有耐心。我再加两条。第一，先分清你手上哪些事是可以重来的，哪些是不能重来的。可以重来的就大胆试，试错的成本就是学费；不能重来的——签的字、押上去的房子、身体——就慢，慢到你自己都嫌烦为止。**可逆的地方大胆，不可逆的地方慢，这一条比任何关于时代的判断都管用。**第二，不懂不做。看不懂的行业别因为它今年最热就冲进去，那不叫抓住时势，那叫替别人抬轿子。有人问我怎么知道自己懂没懂——很简单：你能不能用大白话跟一个外行讲清楚它靠什么赚钱，讲不清楚就是不懂。**最后一句：错过不是错，做错才是错。**时势这东西，一辈子总会来几次；你只要那时候还在场上、还有子弹，就够了。
posts.text_en: Let me say the plainest thing. By the end of this argument everyone agrees on one point: changing yourself is slow, changing your surroundings is faster, and both need patience. I will add two. First, sort what is in front of you into what can be redone and what cannot. Where it can be redone, try boldly — the cost of the error is tuition. Where it cannot — a signature, the house you put up, your body — go slow, slow enough that you get bored of your own caution. **Be bold where the door swings both ways and slow where it does not; that single rule is more useful than any judgement about the era.** Second, if you don't understand it, don't do it. Do not pile into an industry you cannot read because it is the hottest thing this year — that is not catching the moment, that is carrying someone else's sedan chair. People ask how you know whether you understand something. Simple: can you explain in plain words to a layman how it makes money? If you cannot, you don't. **And last: missing out is not a mistake; doing the wrong thing is.** The moment comes round a few times in any life. You only need to still be in the game, with something left to bet, when it does.

summaries.summary: 八个人吵完，共识比预想的多：没有人真主张『天性不可改所以认命』，也没有人主张『只要够努力就能改造自己』。**大家实际落在同一处——改变确实很难，但难点不在意志，在你每天回到的那个触发你的环境。**分歧有三支。一支争这道题问的是谁：马基雅维利说的是退不了场的君主，段永平说的是能换赛道的普通人，两边的答案本来就不该一样。一支争解释与指南的区别：塔勒布指出所有『匹配时代』的证据都是从赢家名单往回读的，作为巅峰的解释成立，作为普通人的指南有毒。第三支争改变的机制：尼采要一次痛的断裂，伍德要连续的低摩擦改造，世亲说两者都要，还得熬过中间那段变淡而未断的时间。
summaries.summary_en: By the end of eight people arguing, the agreement runs deeper than expected: nobody actually defends 'nature cannot change, so resign yourself', and nobody defends 'try hard enough and you can remake yourself'. **They land on the same spot — change really is hard, but the difficulty lies not in will and instead in the environment you return to every day, the one that fires you.** From there it forks three ways. Over who the question is even about: Machiavelli is describing a prince who cannot withdraw, Duan Yongping an ordinary person who can switch arenas, and their answers were never going to match. Over the difference between an explanation and a piece of advice: Taleb points out that every piece of evidence for 'fitting your age' is read backwards off a list of winners — sound as an account of peaks, poisonous as guidance for a life. And over the mechanism of change: Nietzsche wants one clean wound, Wood wants continuous low-friction redesign, and Vasubandhu says both are needed, plus the endurance of the stretch in between where the old force is thinning but not yet gone.
summaries.insight: 把『时代』当成单数，是这场辩论从头到尾的一处算术错误。一个人同时被好几个时钟管着——所在行业的周期、公司的世代、家庭的阶段、身体的年纪，它们几乎从不同步。**多数人说的『生不逢时』，往往不是你和时代错配，是你身上这几个时钟彼此错开了。**行业正在开荒而你家里刚添了孩子；公司进了守成期而你三十五岁正想赌一把。这类错配不需要判断时代，只需要问一句：现在最紧的是哪个时钟？而且它常常可以调——推迟一年、换一个部门、把赌注拆小，都是在给时钟对表。比起猜时代往哪走，这件事既更可控，也更接近人真正卡住的地方。
summaries.insight_en: Treating 'the era' as a singular is an arithmetic mistake that ran through the whole session. Several clocks govern anyone at once — the cycle of their industry, the generation of their company, the stage of their family, the decade of their body — and these are almost never in phase. **What people call being born at the wrong time is usually not a mismatch between you and the age, but a mismatch among your own clocks.** The industry is breaking new ground just as a child arrives at home; the company enters its consolidating stage exactly when you turn thirty-five and want to gamble. Diagnosing this requires no judgement about the era at all, only one question: which clock is tightest right now? And clocks can often be adjusted — postpone a year, move to another division, cut the bet into smaller pieces. Compared with guessing where the age is heading, this is both far more controllable and far closer to where people are actually stuck.
summaries.advice: **这周不必决定你是什么样的人，只需要改动你每天站的那两三个位置。**最省力的一件是做三天线索记录：把你最想改的那个行为，记下每次发生的时间、地点、前一件事、旁边有谁——多数人会发现它只集中在两三个场景，那两三个场景才是要动的东西。接着给自己划一条可逆线：这周的决定分两堆，能重来的当天就定、别再拖；不能重来的（签字、大额、身体、关系）强制过夜，并且提前安排成即使你还是老样子也不至于崩。最后是趁断点动手：换工作、搬家、换班次的头两三周旧线索失效，是重装习惯最便宜的窗口；眼下没有断点，就自己造一个小的——换条通勤路线、换个办公位、把手机放到另一个房间。
summaries.advice_en: **This week you need not decide what kind of person you are; you only need to change the two or three places you stand in each day.** The cheapest move is three days of cue logging: take the behaviour you most want to change and record, each time it happens, the hour, the place, what you had just finished and who was nearby. Most people find it clusters into two or three settings, and those settings are what needs moving. Next, draw yourself a reversibility line: sort this week's decisions into two piles, settle the reversible ones the same day instead of letting them drag, and force the irreversible ones — signatures, large sums, your body, your relationships — to sleep overnight, then arrange them so they hold even if you stay exactly as you are. Last, work with the discontinuities: the first two or three weeks of a new job, a move or a new shift, when the old cues stop working, are the cheapest window for reinstalling a habit. If none is in sight, manufacture a small one — a different commute, a different desk, the phone in another room.

summaries.summary: 人的成败既非纯粹由性格决定，也不是时代单方面的恩赐——这是全场最大的共识；真正可干预的是人与环境的接合方式。压力来临时，人会退回旧习，因此应在平时调整线索、保留余地、避开毁灭性风险，并把长处放进会奖励它的阶段。**与其预测谁造就谁，不如提前安排自己即使判断错了也能继续行动。**真正的分歧在解释层级：历史必然、群体周期、个人意志、习惯机制与随机性回答的是不同问题；落实到行动，则是磨炼自身、选择场域、设计暴露与退路三条路径孰轻孰重。
summaries.insight: 「我适合什么时代」很容易变成事后编写的自我故事：成功一次便说找到了天命，受挫一次又说环境不对。但结果同时受能力、运气、样本量和反馈周期影响，单次成败几乎无法证明适配。**人与时势的匹配应被当作一个待检验的假设，而不是一份性格宣言。**检验时不能只看短期掌声，还要看能否持续产出、是否有人愿意付费或合作、代价能否承受，以及做完后是否愿意再来一轮。真正适合的场域，不只是放大你的长处，也不会靠透支健康、信誉和未来选择来制造成功感。
summaries.advice: 今天先做三件事。第一，把眼前决定分成可逆与不可逆两栏；对负债、健康、长期合同等不可逆事项，先删掉最坏结果。第二，选一个反复困扰你的行为，连续三天记录时间、地点、前置动作和在场的人，再给触发点增减二十秒摩擦。第三，用一周做一个低成本场域实验：投入十小时完成可展示的小项目，事先写下三个指标——是否按时完成、是否获得真实外部反馈、是否愿意继续四周。**先保住下一轮，再用小实验寻找真正会奖励你的地方。**周末按记录决定继续、调整或退出，不凭一次输赢给自己定性。
summaries.summary_en: Outcomes are produced neither by personality alone nor by an era acting on passive individuals — that is the panel's strongest point of agreement. What can actually be changed is the interface between a person and an environment. Under pressure, people revert to practiced routines, so the useful work happens beforehand: redesign cues, preserve room to maneuver, avoid ruinous risks, and place your strengths in a setting or phase that rewards them. **Instead of trying to predict whether the age makes the person or the person makes the age, arrange your life so you can keep acting even when your judgment is wrong.** The real disagreements concern levels of explanation. Historical necessity, collective cycles, individual will, habit mechanisms, and randomness address different parts of the causal chain. In practical terms, the dispute is mainly about emphasis: whether to reshape yourself, select a better arena, or engineer your exposure and exit options. Those approaches are not mutually exclusive, but they operate on different timelines.
summaries.insight_en: The claim that a person has found the right era is often a story written after the result. One success is treated as proof of destiny; one setback becomes proof that the environment was wrong. Yet any outcome mixes skill, luck, sample size, and the length of the feedback cycle, so a single win or loss reveals very little about fit. **Person–era fit should be treated as a hypothesis to test, not as a declaration of identity.** A sound test looks beyond immediate applause. Ask whether you can produce consistently, whether real people will pay, cooperate, or rely on the result, whether the costs are bearable, and whether you would willingly repeat the effort. Some environments reward a trait in the short run while quietly consuming health, reputation, or future options. That is exploitation, not durable fit. The right arena does more than magnify a strength: it allows that strength to compound without requiring you to destroy the foundations of the next round.
summaries.advice_en: Do three things today. First, divide your current decisions into reversible and irreversible ones. For debt, health, long contracts, or anything else that is hard to undo, remove the catastrophic downside before seeking upside. Second, choose one recurring behavior you want to change and track it for three days: time, place, preceding action, and who is present. Then add or remove twenty seconds of friction at the trigger point. Third, run a one-week, low-cost arena test. Spend ten hours producing something visible—a prototype, analysis, lesson, sales attempt, or short project—and define three measures in advance: whether you finished on time, whether you received genuine external feedback, and whether you would continue for four more weeks. **Protect your chance to play the next round, then use small experiments to find the places that genuinely reward you.** At week’s end, continue, modify, or exit based on the record rather than using one result to define who you are.

summaries.summary: 全场最终达成的深刻共识在于：**在风暴降临的临界时刻试图强行扭转天性纯属幻想，真正的生机永远来自风暴来临前对场域、风险敞口与生活环境的主动重塑。**无论持唯物、历史、行为学还是唯识论立场，诸位皆认同选场与改境的效能远胜于临阵磨枪。真正的根本分歧在于主客体的因果权重：黑格尔与赫勒敦将个体视作时代意志或代际周期的被动载体与分母；尼采、塔勒布与段永平则坚信主体的自主能动性——区别仅在于究竟是用强韧意志冲破均值，还是靠严守能力圈与凸性结构在时代的随机波动中安身立命。
summaries.insight: 整场辩论潜意识里仍将“时势”预设为一个均质、统一的宏大浪潮，但现代社会的真实时势早已碎裂为无数异构且不同步的局部网络。**决定一个人际遇的往往不是抽象的宏观大势，而是你在极小尺度上与哪一个微观生态共生。**许多事后被加冕为“踩准时代”的样本，起初不过是在宏大叙事的边缘搭建了一个反直觉的微小生境。时代的宏观走势不可预测且对普通人极不友好，与其费尽心力去猜下个风口在哪，不如在局部建立某种不可替代的怪异优势——让时代在碎裂中撞上你，而不是你去追赶时代的幻影。
summaries.advice: 普通人本周即可落地的三项动作：第一，践行塔勒布与段永平的防御逻辑，清查个人财务与职场中的单点毁灭风险，**对任何可能让你彻底出局的杠杆与协议坚决说不，守住不可逆底线**；第二，运用伍德的二十秒阻力法则，把你最想戒除的行为在物理链条上增加一道微小摩擦，把发挥你优势的工具直接置于视线正中央；第三，停止宏观择时，列出三个能够包容你固有性格缺陷的细分小圈子，以极低沉没成本进行为期两周的试探，寻找能为你这副脾气提供正向定价的微环境。
summaries.summary_en: The ultimate consensus of the debate is striking: **attempting to forcefully alter one's ingrained nature during a crisis is pure folly; genuine agency lies in reshaping one's environment, exposure, and friction long before the storm hits.** Whether viewing through historical materialism, behaviorism, or Yogacara philosophy, all agree that choosing the right arena far outweighs eleventh-hour self-reformation. The core divergence lies in causal priority: Hegel and Ibn Khaldun treat the individual as an ephemeral vessel or demographic denominator of historical cycles, whereas Nietzsche, Taleb, and Duan emphasize personal agency—differing on whether to forge destiny via sovereign will or to survive systemic randomness through convex positioning and disciplined boundaries.
summaries.insight_en: The roundtable subtly presupposes the "times" as a monolithic, homogeneous tide, whereas modern reality is a constellation of fragmented, desynchronized micro-networks. **What governs personal trajectory is rarely an abstract historical epoch, but the specific micro-niche one co-evolves with at an intimate scale.** Most figures retroactively crowned as "riding the wave" merely carved out an eccentric sanctuary on the margins of mainstream trends. Macro trends are unpredictable and largely indifferent to ordinary people; rather than exhausting yourself chasing the next zeitgeist, cultivate localized pricing power where your idiosyncratic traits are recognized as unfair advantages.
summaries.advice_en: Three actionable steps for this week: First, apply Taleb and Duan's defensive filter by auditing personal finances and career dependencies, **ruthlessly eliminating any single point of failure or leverage that could permanently take you out of the game**; second, deploy Wood's twenty-second rule by adding physical friction to your worst default habits while placing tools that amplify your natural edge in plain sight; third, halt grand macro-speculation and identify three micro-communities that reward your exact disposition, running low-cost two-week probes to find an environment that naturally prices your traits as strengths.

hooks.text: **几个不对表的时钟**：人被默认只处在一个时代里，可行业的周期、公司的世代、家庭的阶段、身体的年纪几乎从不同步。所谓生不逢时，往往是这几个时钟彼此错开——行业正在开荒而家里刚添了孩子，公司进了守成期而你正想赌一把。这里有一个还没被拆开的可能：错配若主要发生在时钟之间而不是人与时代之间，那么可调的旋钮就比想象中多得多，推迟一年、换一个部门、把赌注拆小，都是在对表。
hooks.text_en: **Clocks that are out of phase**: a person is assumed to occupy one era, yet the cycle of an industry, the generation of a company, the stage of a family and the decade of a body are almost never in sync. What gets called being born at the wrong time is often those clocks running out of phase — the industry breaking new ground exactly as a child arrives, the company consolidating exactly when you want to gamble. An unopened possibility sits here: if the mismatch happens mostly between clocks rather than between a person and an age, then there are far more adjustable dials than anyone assumed, and postponing a year, changing division or cutting the bet smaller are all ways of resetting them.

hooks.text: **不发言的那半个样本**：所有关于风格与时代匹配的证据都是从赢家名单往回读的，同样莽撞、同样在奖励莽撞的年月出手、然后被一场瘟疫抹掉的人不在数据里。可如果那半个样本原则上取不到，我们该拿这条规律怎么办——是彻底弃用，还是只把它当成事后叙事而绝不当作事前指南？有没有一种办法，能从失败者留下的痕迹里把对照组补回来一部分？
hooks.text_en: **The half of the sample that never speaks**: every piece of evidence about style-era fit is read backwards off a list of winners, while the men who were equally headlong, struck in an equally headlong age, and were erased by a plague are absent from the data. If that half of the sample is unobtainable in principle, what should be done with the rule — discard it outright, or admit it strictly as retrospective narrative and never as prospective advice? Is there any way to reconstruct part of the control group from the traces losers do leave behind?

hooks.text: **断点是稀缺资源**：搬家、换工作、换城市之后旧线索失效的那两三周，是一生中最容易重装习惯的窗口。可这种窗口一辈子只有有限的几个，而且往往在人最忙乱的时候到来，于是被整箱整箱的搬家纸盒吃掉。这就把它变成了一项该提前规划的资源——想改的三件事排好队等下一个断点，比在稳定期反复发愿更接近可行；而人造的小断点（换通勤路线、换办公位）究竟能替代多少，目前还是一段空白。
hooks.text_en: **Discontinuities are a scarce resource**: the two or three weeks after a move, a new job or a new city, when the old cues stop working, are the easiest window in a life for reinstalling habits. A life contains only a handful of them, they tend to arrive when a person is most overwhelmed, and they get eaten by cardboard boxes. That makes them something to plan for — queueing up the three things you want to change for the next one is far more workable than renewing a vow through a stable stretch, while how much a manufactured small discontinuity (a new commute, a new desk) can substitute remains an open blank.

hooks.text: **给你所在的地方估一个世代**：建立期奖励能忍受混乱的人，守成期奖励能把混乱变成流程的人；同一副脾气换个阶段，就从骨气变成不合群。可多数人从来没有为自己所在的公司、行业、城市估过这个阶段，于是把一个结构性的错配长年当成个人努力不够。到底该看哪几件事才估得准，估完了又只有哪几个动作可选？
hooks.text_en: **Estimate the generation of the place you are in**: the founding stage rewards those who can tolerate disorder, the consolidating stage those who can turn disorder into process, and the same temper moved between them turns from backbone into not fitting in. Yet most people have never estimated that stage for their own company, industry or city, and so spend years booking a structural mismatch as personal laziness. What exactly should you look at to estimate it, and once you have, how many moves are actually available?

answer.lead: **世代不是公司的年龄，是它的奖励结构。**同一家公司，不同部门可以处在不同的世代，所以要估的是你每天待的那个单位、不是财报上的成立年份。下面几条各看一眼，哪一列勾得多就是哪一列。

head: 看什么
还在建立期（奖励能扛混乱的人）
已进守成期（奖励能把混乱变成流程的人）
rows: 开荒：没人做过的事，没有说明书
补漏：接手已有流程，填别人留下的坑
能把事做成的人，过程难看也认
不出错的人，流程漂亮优先
怕来不及，怕被别人先做了

answer.tail: 勾完只有两个动作：**要么去那个正在奖励你这副脾气的阶段，要么留下并认下你要付的代价。**最坏的是留在一个不奖励你的阶段，还每天怪自己不够努力。另外两条提醒：估的是部门不是公司，同一栋楼里两层可以完全不同；守成期也不等于坏，它只是奖励另一种人——如果你正好是把混乱变成流程的那种，它就是你的建立期。

answer_en.lead: **A generation is not a company's age; it is its reward structure.** Two divisions of the same firm can sit in different generations, so estimate the unit you actually spend your days in, not the founding year on the annual report. Run down the rows below; whichever column you tick more often is the one you are in.

head: What to look at
Still founding (rewards those who tolerate disorder)
Now consolidating (rewards those who turn disorder into process)
rows: Open ground: things nobody has done, no manual
Patching leaks: inheriting a process, filling someone's hole
Those who get it done, ugly process forgiven
Those who make no mistakes, clean process first
How it was won back then
How the rules were set back then
Start, then get it ratified afterwards
Being too late, being beaten to it
Is called gutsy and given resources
Is called a poor fit and given training

answer_en.tail: Once you have ticked the rows there are only two moves: **go to the stage that is currently rewarding your temper, or stay and accept the price.** The worst option is staying in a stage that does not reward you while blaming yourself daily for not trying hard enough. Two cautions: estimate the division, not the company — two floors of one building can differ completely; and consolidating is not the bad column, it simply rewards a different person. If you are the one who turns disorder into process, it is your founding stage.

hooks.text: **变淡而未断的那一段**：旧习气断了触发它的情境之后，力量会慢慢变薄却不会立刻断；多数人正是在这段既没有旧回报、又还没建立新回报的空档里回到老路上。这一段该怎么过——靠什么标记进度，靠什么撑住？把复发当作失败，与把复发当作过程的一部分，会带来完全不同的结果吗？
hooks.text_en: **The stretch where it thins but has not ended**: once an old habit loses the setting that fired it, its force fades slowly rather than stopping at once, and most people go back to the old road precisely in that gap — the old reward gone, the new one not yet established. How should that stretch be crossed: what marks progress, and what holds a person through it? Does treating a relapse as failure, rather than as part of the process, produce a materially different outcome?
